[Document 1]
The present analysis compares two palliative treatment concepts for lung cancer in terms of overall survival.

[Document 2]
Few studies have assessed whether the advantage chemotherapy has been shown to have in treating advanced non-small lung carcinoma in clinical trials is transferrable to normal health care activity. This could explain the skepticism of a large number of pneumologists towards this treatment. The objective of our study was to analyze prognostic factors related to survival and to see whether cytostatic treatment was an independent predictor.

[Document 3]
This study is limited by its retrospective nature and heterogeneous radiotherapy regimes among radiotherapy patients.

[Document 4]
It remains controversial whether there is a gender difference in survival of patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer.

[Document 5]
Treatment of elderly cancer patients has gained importance. One question regarding the treatment of metastatic spinal cord compression (MSCC) is whether elderly patients benefit from surgery in addition to radiotherapy? In attempting to answer this question, we performed a matched-pair analysis comparing surgery followed by radiotherapy to radiotherapy alone.

passages.passage_body: The present analysis compares two palliative treatment concepts for lung cancer in terms of overall survival.

Few studies have assessed whether the advantage chemotherapy has been shown to have in treating advanced non-small lung carcinoma in clinical trials is transferrable to normal health care activity. This could explain the skepticism of a large number of pneumologists towards this treatment. The objective of our study was to analyze prognostic factors related to survival and to see whether cytostatic treatment was an independent predictor.
This study is limited by its retrospective nature and heterogeneous radiotherapy regimes among radiotherapy patients.
It remains controversial whether there is a gender difference in survival of patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer.

Treatment of elderly cancer patients has gained importance. One question regarding the treatment of metastatic spinal cord compression (MSCC) is whether elderly patients benefit from surgery in addition to radiotherapy? In attempting to answer this question, we performed a matched-pair analysis comparing surgery followed by radiotherapy to radiotherapy alone.
